function: One in-context transformer solves multi-user precoding (sum-rate and max-min SINR, via predicted power parameters) and one-step downlink channel prediction (pp. 3-5, 8).
system: Single-cell downlink MU-MISO-OFDM: BS UPA 4x4, K=4 single-antenna users at 10-100 km/h; 2.4 GHz, 8.64 MHz, 48 subcarriers; no RIS (p. 8).
method: Decoder-only LLaMA-style transformer (4 layers, 4 heads, d=512) trained from scratch on three tasks; supervised with WMMSE and Schubert-Boche labels; in-context learning, no per-task fine-tuning (pp. 3, 6-8).
data_channel: QuaDRiGa generator, 3GPP TR 38.901 UMa NLOS, 21 clusters with 20 paths, 2.4 GHz; synthetic; 100,000 samples per configuration, split 8:1:1 (pp. 8-9).
test_conditions: Training: SNR 0/10/20/30 dB, speeds 10/40/70/100 km/h. Testing adds unseen SNR 5/15/25 dB and speeds 20/30/50 km/h, using 4 demonstration pairs (pp. 9-10).
baselines: Classical: WMMSE (sum rate), Schubert-Boche (max-min SINR), outdated CSI (prediction). Learned: CNN-based BNN [11] (matched and fixed variants), LLM4CP [20] (pp. 9-10).
metrics: Sum rate (precoding P1), minimum user rate (P2), NMSE of the predicted channel (P3), versus SNR or velocity and number of demonstration pairs (pp. 9-11).
q1_support: p. 8: "we utilize the QuaDRiGa channel generator [40]"; p. 8: "We specifically adopt the 3GPP Urban Macro (UMa) channel model"
q2_support: p. 10: "crucially including intermediate velocities (e.g., 20, 30, 50 km/h) that were unseen during the training phase"
q3_support: p. 9: "we employ the classical WMMSE algorithm [41] and a CNN-based Beamforming Neural Network (BNN) [11]"; p. 10: "First, we employ the LLM4CP model [20]"
q4_support: p. 8: "the model employs 4 layers, 4 attention heads, an embedding dimension of 512, and a FFN dimension of 1024"; p. 11: "enhancing its computational efficiency for edge deployment through model compression" is future work; no parameter count, operations or runtime is reported.
q5_support: p. 8: "we utilize the QuaDRiGa channel generator [40]"; the data are generated by the authors, and the paper gives no code or data link.
notes: PDF is the arXiv version 2507.18167v2 (12 Jan 2026). Page 1 shows no DOI, so the match with 10.1109/tcomm.2026.3655778 rests on title and content only; nothing contradicts it. Area 3 because two of the three tasks (P1 sum rate, P2 max-min SINR) are precoding and the headline metrics are rates; the third task is channel prediction (area 2), so the reviewer may prefer 2. q2 is borderline: the unseen points are speeds 20, 30, 50 km/h (p. 10) and SNR 5, 15, 25 dB (p. 9), all interpolated inside the training range with the same UMa NLOS setup, antennas and users; SNR points alone would not count, so q2 rests on the speeds and the reviewer should confirm. q3 uses BNN [11] and LLM4CP [20] as learned baselines and WMMSE, Schubert-Boche and outdated CSI as non-learned, on sum rate (Fig. 9), minimum rate (Fig. 10) and NMSE (Fig. 11). p. 3 calls the training self-supervised, but p. 8 uses WMMSE and Schubert-Boche outputs as supervised labels.
